transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-25 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Torres (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Marina Lopez (AlphaMed - Head of Security), Evan Chu (AlphaMed - Platform Eng), Priya Shah (AlphaMed - Legal)

[00:00] Lena (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Lena, I'll own the account. Samir's our SE, he'll walk through the tech details.
[00:12] Marina (AlphaMed): Thanks, Lena. We want to focus today on data residency, region pinning, and cross-border processing — we've got some regulatory constraints for EU patient data.
[00:20] Samir (Redwood SE): Great, yeah, we'll cover architecture options — hosted, dedicated, private — and how region pinning works, plus KMS and audit logs. Quick note: transcription may scramble some product names, sorry in advance.
[00:35] Evan (AlphaMed): That's fine. High level, our requirements: EU patient data must not leave EU for processing, we also need audit trails for access and model outputs retained 7 years for compliance.
[00:50] Priya (Legal): And from legal: need DPA and confirmation of transfer mechanisms — SCCs or adequacy decisions — and list of sub-processors.
[01:05] Lena: Understood. At a high level, Redwood supports three deployment modes. Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Private (VPC / on-prem). For EU-only processing we can do region pinning on both Dedicated and Hosted with routing policies, and Private can be entirely customer-controlled.
[01:25] Marina: Can you be more specific about hosted? We are wary that hosted might route some requests through US infra even if customers are in EU.
[01:32] Samir: Yeah, good question. With our Hosted API we have region selection at the API endpoint level — "eu-west-1" etc — and routing tries to keep processing within the region. There are caveats though: certain background services, telemetry, or control-plane metadata might be processed in our control plane which today is multi-region. For the strictest residency controls we recommend Dedicated with regional-only compute or Private.
[01:55] Marina: When you say control-plane metadata, is that anything like prompts or model outputs? We need to be sure those do not leave the EU.
[02:05] Samir: Right — the customer data plane (model inference) can be pinned to EU compute; however control-plane logs and metrics might include meta identifiers. We can redact or configure that. If you require zero cross-border data, Private (VPC or on-prem) is the only option we can guarantee — because you run the control plane or we provide a customer-managed control plane.
[02:25] Evan: For Dedicated, is there an SLA to keep processing in region and no cross-border fallback?
[02:30] Samir: Dedicated instances can be provisioned with strict region affinity. We can set a policy to avoid automatic fallback to other regions. That said, we need to bake that into the contract and the deployment plan — otherwise automatic fallback to compatible model variants can occur if capacity is exhausted.
[02:45] Priya: On transfer mechanisms: do you support Standard Contract Clauses (SCCs) and can you share a DPA?
[02:52] Lena: Yes, we provide a DPA and use SCCs for EU transfers. We'll share our standard DPA and SCC language; legal can review and request redlines.
[03:05] Marina: Sub-processors — who are you using? If it's major cloud providers, can we get an explicit list and confirmation they have EU regions?
[03:12] Samir: Primary sub-processors are AWS (eu-west-1, eu-central-1), GCP (europe-west), and a managed storage provider. We will share a current sub-processor list; it's typically updated quarterly.
[03:28] Marina: Audit logs — we need immutable logs with retention controls and exported to our SIEM. Can you push logs to our S3 in EU or to our SIEM via syslog?
[03:40] Samir: Yes, audit logs can be configured to ship to customer endpoints; for Hosted we support pushing to customer S3 (region-bound), and we have webhooks / syslog connectors for SIEM ingest. For Private, logs are fully customer-managed.
[03:55] Evan: Encryption and keys — do you offer customer-managed keys? If we put patient PII through inference, keys must be ours.
[04:02] Samir: We support BYOK via KMS in Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we offer a KMS integration where you can bring keys in supported clouds; the key material stays in KMS, we call APIs to decrypt in region. We can also offer HSM-backed keys for enterprise plans.
[04:20] Marina: Is ephemeral caching used? We want to ensure KV cache or prefix cache doesn't leak across tenants or regions.
[04:29] Samir: Our runtime uses KV caches per tenant and per model shard; we isolate per tenant. For strict compliance we can disable cross-tenant caching and ensure caches are scoped to region. There are some performance trade-offs but it's doable.
[04:45] Lena: Quick interjection — AlphaMed, do you have a preference between Dedicated or Private route?
[04:50] Marina: We're leaning Dedicated in EU region first, maybe move to Private for very sensitive workloads. But we'd like to understand the differences in guarantees and pricing.
[04:58] Samir: Pricing aside, Dedicated gives you predictable capacity and we can implement region affinity; Private gives the strongest assurances because control plane and data plane are customer-managed. We'll include a side-by-side doc in the follow-up.
[05:10] Priya: Regarding auditability — can Redwood provide access logs for model prompts as part of the audit? We need to know who called which prompt, when, and what model version was used.
[05:20] Samir: Yes, we capture request metadata including account id, API key, truncated prompt hash (we can exclude full prompt by request), model version, latency, and processing region. Full prompt capture is configurable — default is truncated for privacy. We can enable full capture for compliance but that increases storage and PII handling concerns.
[05:40] Evan: For EU-only workloads, if we enable full prompt capture, can the storage be enforced to stay in EU?
[05:46] Samir: Yes — storage buckets are in-region and we can configure retention policies. We'll provide configuration examples for retention TTL and export to your SIEM.
[05:55] Marina: Cross-border processing: what about human review or safety team? Any content routed to CA/US humans for moderation?
[06:02] Lena: We do not outsource human review of customer prompts unless explicitly enabled; for hosted safety telemetry we use anonymized signals. For enterprise deals we can opt-out of any human-in-the-loop features.
[06:14] Priya: We also need to confirm that subprocessors processing metadata do not include US-based analytics unless we opt in.
[06:20] Samir: Correct; we can restrict analytics collection to EU processors for your account. That will be part of the account configuration and flagged in the deployment.
[06:30] Marina: Can you talk about the legal mechanisms: do you accept EU SCCs and do you have a Data Processing Addendum?
[06:36] Lena: Yes and yes. We'll attach our DPA and the standard SCCs. If you need alternative transfer mechanisms (e.g., UK adequacy), we can discuss specifics.
[06:48] Evan: Operationally, how does region pinning get configured? Is it an account-level flag or per-route?
[06:55] Samir: It's flexible: account-level default region, per-route overrides, and model-level routing rules. You can pin routes to eu-west-1 and enforce no-fallback. We'll send a sample config snippet with our followup.
[07:10] Marina: About failures: if eu region is down, will requests queue or fail? We can't have silent fallback to other regions.
[07:18] Samir: We can set the policy to fail closed — requests will fail with a 5xx if region unavailable; we also support queueing behavior but for strict residency we recommend fail-closed.
[07:30] Evan: How about latency when we use dedicated smaller pools? Any data on per-token latency in eu-west-1 vs global?
[07:38] Samir: We'll share benchmarks; rough numbers: for 8k context Llama-ish models we see p50 latency ~120ms per token on our dedicated A100-like pools, eu numbers typically add 10-20ms network overhead vs us-west. We'll include a benchmark spreadsheet.
[07:54] Lena: I'll attach the benchmarks and the region-pinning design doc after the call.
[08:00] Marina: One security question — RBAC and SSO: can we integrate SAML with SCIM to sync user groups, and apply RBAC scoped to projects with audit trails?
[08:09] Samir: Yes — SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning available for enterprise plans. RBAC is project and role based, and all auth events are logged. We can show RBAC examples in the SE deep dive.
[08:22] Priya: For legal: we want to ensure we can audit access to keys and admin actions in the control plane. Are admin actions logged and exportable?
[08:30] Samir: Admin actions, change history, and key management operations are logged and can be exported via syslog or stored in customer S3. For Private deployments, audit trails are entirely under your control.
[08:44] Marina: Ok, let's talk about sub-processors list and any third-party ML infra partners.
[08:49] Samir: We use a set of third-party infra partners for GPU jobs, but the compute for live inference is on our managed clusters in the region and in clouds listed. We'll provide names and roles in the sub-processor list.
[09:05] Evan: Is there encryption in transit end-to-end? TLS plus mTLS for backend?
[09:10] Samir: All traffic is TLS; for private peering we support mTLS and private link type connections. Keys are rotated per our security policy, and we can coordinate key rotations with your KMS.
[09:22] Marina: Data retention policy — default retention for logs and prompts? We need to be able to configure 7-year retention for audit logs and 90-day for prompts unless otherwise specified.
[09:32] Samir: Defaults are 90 days for request bodies and 1 year for logs. But for enterprise customers, retention policies are configurable and can be extended to your requested 7 years for logs. We'll provide the config options.
[09:48] Lena: Quick pause — any additional regulatory constraints, e.g., specific European countries that have extra rules?
[09:55] Marina: We're primarily Germany and Spain. Data residency rules are pretty strict; Germany is conservative about transfers.
[10:03] Samir: Noted; we'll include country-specific notes.
[10:08] Priya: About contractual clauses — will you accept audit rights or right to inspect sub-processor compliance?
[10:15] Lena: We can provide SOC2 reports and work with you on reasonable audit rights; for sub-processors we provide attestation and can support audits for enterprise customers under NDA.
[10:28] Evan: For the PoC, we want a small dedicated capacity in eu-west-1 serving a single model. We need to run throughput and verify no cross-border calls.
[10:36] Samir: Sounds good; we'll scope a PoC: dedicated pool in eu-west-1, sample data residency tests, log forwarding to your SIEM, and KMS integration.
[10:45] Marina: Can we get an architecture diagram showing data plane and control plane flows and which components may be US-located?
[10:52] Samir: Absolutely, will include that. We'll mark which control plane services remain in US control plane and how we can move them or provide a customer-managed control plane.
[11:05] Lena: For the follow-up: I'll send SOC2 / ISO artifacts and the DPA; Samir will send region pinning config and PoC scope; Priya you'll review DPA and propose redlines.
[11:16] Priya: Yes, we'll review and get back in the week.
[11:20] Marina: One last quick thing — cross-border subprocessors like analytics, do you allow us to opt-out?
[11:26] Samir: We can opt-out of analytics collection and restrict telemetry to EU sub-processors for your account.
[11:33] Evan: Great. On monitoring, will we get per-request cost and token telemetry? We need to ensure billing data doesn't expose prompts.
[11:41] Samir: Billing-level metrics are aggregated; per-request cost is available as metadata but without full prompt bodies unless enabled. We can also provide token-level aggregates.
[11:52] Lena: OK, sounds like we have a plan. Any other questions?
[11:56] Marina: Not from me. We'll wait for the docs.
[12:00] Priya: Thanks everyone.
[12:02] Lena: Thanks, we'll follow up with artifacts and schedule the SE deep dive.
[12:06] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mislabels and dropped punctuation; some vendor names may be slightly off.
